A montage illustration showing the elements of early Nigerian nationalism: on the left, a vintage printing press producing a copy of the "West African Pilot" newspaper with a headline demanding self-rule; on the right, a crowd of workers and market women holding placards during a peaceful protest.

A horizontal timeline from 1922 to 1960 showing key milestones in Nigeria's constitutional development. 1922: Clifford Constitution (Elective Principle). 1946: Richards Constitution (Regionalism). 1951: Macpherson Constitution (Quasi-Federalism). 1954: Lyttelton Constitution (True Federalism). 1957-1958: Constitutional Conferences. 1960: Independence.

A map of Nigeria in 1946 showing the three regions created by the Richards Constitution. The country is divided into the large Northern Region (coloured green), the Western Region (yellow), and the Eastern Region (blue). Lagos is marked as a small dot in the southwest. A bold boundary line separates the North from the South.
